signature: SUBROUTINE ZTGSY2( TRANS, IJOB, M, N, A, LDA, B, LDB, C, LDC, D,

params.name: trans
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: solve the generalized Sylvester equation (1).
-   `= 'T'`: solve the 'transposed' system (3).

params.name: ijob
params.reference:
Specifies what kind of functionality to be performed.

-   `=0`: solve (1) only.
-   `=1`: A contribution from this subsystem to a Frobenius norm-based estimate of the separation between two matrix pairs is computed. (look ahead strategy is used).
-   `=2`: A contribution from this subsystem to a Frobenius norm-based estimate of the separation between two matrix pairs is computed. (DGECON on sub-systems is used.) Not referenced if `TRANS = 'T'`.

params.name: M
params.reference: On entry, M specifies the order of A and D, and the row dimension of C, F, R and L.

params.name: N
params.reference: On entry, N specifies the order of B and E, and the column dimension of C, F, R and L.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, A contains an upper triangular matrix.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, B contains an upper triangular matrix.

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1, N)$.

params.name: C
params.reference: On entry, C contains the right-hand-side of the first matrix equation in (1). On exit, if `IJOB = 0`, C has been overwritten by the solution R.

params.name: ldc
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix C. $\mathrm{LDC} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: D
params.reference: On entry, D contains an upper triangular matrix.

params.name: ldd
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix D. $\mathrm{LDD} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: E
params.reference: On entry, E contains an upper triangular matrix.

params.name: lde
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix E. $\mathrm{LDE} \ge \max (1, N)$.

params.name: F
params.reference: On entry, F contains the right-hand-side of the second matrix equation in (1). On exit, if `IJOB = 0`, F has been overwritten by the solution L.

params.name: ldf
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix F. $\mathrm{LDF} \ge \max (1, M)$.

params.name: scale
params.reference: On exit, $0 \le \mathrm{SCALE} \le 1$. If $0 < \mathrm{SCALE} < 1$, the solutions R and L (C and F on entry) will hold the solutions to a slightly perturbed system but the input matrices A, B, D and E have not been changed. If `SCALE = 0`, R and L will hold the solutions to the homogeneous system with $C = F = 0$. Normally, `SCALE = 1`.

params.name: rdsum
params.reference: On entry, the sum of squares of computed contributions to the Dif-estimate under computation by ZTGSYL, where the scaling factor `RDSCAL` (see below) has been factored out. On exit, the corresponding sum of squares updated with the contributions from the current sub-system. If `TRANS = 'T'` `RDSUM` is not touched. NOTE: `RDSUM` only makes sense when ZTGSY2 is called by ZTGSYL.

params.name: rdscal
params.reference: On entry, scaling factor used to prevent overflow in `RDSUM`. On exit, `RDSCAL` is updated w.r.t. the current contributions in `RDSUM`. If `TRANS = 'T'`, `RDSCAL` is not touched. NOTE: `RDSCAL` only makes sense when ZTGSY2 is called by ZTGSYL.

params.name: info
params.reference:
On exit, if `INFO` is set to

-   `=0`: Successful exit
-   `<0`: If `INFO = -i`, input argument number i is illegal.
-   `>0`: The matrix pairs (A, D) and (B, E) have common or very close eigenvalues.
